title: Reporting what people say using nouns and adjectives

sections.title: Reporting using nouns
sections.content:
We sometimes report people's words and thoughts using a noun in the reporting clause followed by a reported clause beginning with that, a to-infinitive-, or wh-word. Most of these nouns are related to reporting verbs (acknowledgement – acknowledge, statement – state, etc.). Note that when we report using nouns and adjectives the exact original words are not necessarily reported.
Noun + that-clause:
• The claim is often made that smoking causes heart disease.
• The jury came to the conclusion that the woman was guilty.
Also: acknowledgement, advice, allegation, announcement, answer, argument, comment, decision, explanation, forecast, guarantee, indication, observation, promise, recommendation, reply, speculation, statement, suggestion, threat, warning
Noun + to-infinitive clause:
• I accepted Luisa's invitation to visit her in Rome.

exercises.question: The turning point in his life came when he took the ___ (become - actor)
options: decision to become an actor / that he would become an actor
exercises.hint: Use a to-infinitive or that-clause after 'decision'.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: decision to become an actor / that he would become an actor
We use would here for past habits, hypothetical situations, or reported speech.
💡 Use a to-infinitive or that-clause after 'decision'.

exercises.sentence: She made a suggestion of trying a completely different approach to the problem.
exercises.correction: She made a suggestion that we try a completely different approach to the problem.
acceptable: made a suggestion that we should try
exercises.hint: 'A suggestion that + subjunctive clause' or 'a suggestion to + infinitive' — not 'suggestion of -ing'.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: made a suggestion that we try
The noun 'suggestion' takes: (1) 'suggestion that + bare subjunctive': 'suggestion that we try'; (2) 'suggestion to + infinitive': 'suggestion to try a new approach'. The pattern 'suggestion of + gerund' is not standard in formal written English for reporting proposals.

exercises.question: He failed to address the ___ (who - pay - repairs - building)
options: issue of who pays for repairs to the building
issue who will pay for repairs to the building
exercises.explanation:
Answer: issue who will pay for repairs to the building
Use a wh-clause after 'issue'. Use will here — this is neither a fixed timetable event (which would take the present simple) nor a pre-planned personal arrangement (which would take the present continuous or be going to).

exercises.sentence: He expressed his refusal to attending the compulsory training session.
exercises.correction: He expressed his refusal to attend the compulsory training session.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: refusal to attend
Reporting nouns that express decisions or stances (refusal, decision, intention, desire, wish, agreement, offer, promise) are followed by 'to + bare infinitive', not 'to + gerund'. 'Refusal to attending' wrongly adds -ing after 'to'. Always: refusal to do, decision to go, intention to leave.

exercises.question: I was delighted to get an ___ (spend the holidays - them - Scotland)
options: invitation to spend the holidays with them in Scotland
invitation that I spend the holidays
exercises.explanation:
Answer: invitation to spend the holidays with them in Scotland
Use a to-infinitive after 'invitation'. The grammatical signals in this sentence — the key words, connectors, or context — require this specific form. Look for these signals to make the same choice independently.

exercises.question: The doctors expressed ___ that the patient would make a full recovery.
exercises.hint: A reporting adjective-to-noun conversion: 'They were confident' → 'They expressed confidence'.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: confidence / hope / optimism
Reporting with nouns: 'expressed + noun' conveys attitude. Key reporting nouns: confidence (that), doubt (about/that), concern (about/that), hope (that), certainty (that), belief (that), insistence (that). These can replace clause structures: 'She was confident' → 'She expressed confidence'.

exercises.question: At the end the writers suggest when it is appropriate to correct students' grammar mistakes. -> The writers end with ___
options: suggestions as to when it is appropriate to correct students' grammar mistakes.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: suggestions as to when it is appropriate to correct students' grammar mistakes.
Noun + as to + wh-word.

exercises.question: People have argued a great deal about how to define poverty. -> There has been ___
options: argument as to how to define poverty.
an argument about how defining poverty.
argument that how poverty is defined.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: argument as to how to define poverty.
Noun + as to + wh-clause.
